clue.text: Old warhorses don't pay out cash!

definitions.meaning: horses ridden into battle by knights in former times
those who put purchases on account or on a card rather than paying in notes

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: people who charge goods to an account are not paying cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight's battle steed was a charger, and someone who puts things on account charges them instead of handing over money.

clue.text: Splashdown!

parts.note: not a spacecraft landing in the sea but water itself crashing down a steep drop

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation reads like a space-capsule landing; split it as 'splash down' and it describes a great waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A large waterfall, where a river plunges over a sheer drop, is literally water splashing down.

clue.text: Pop back in place repaired device

indicators.note: back tells us the word for father is to be read the other way round

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father, PA

indicators.note: something repaired has been put back together, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to put Dad back where he was, after fixing a household gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PA into AP; 'repaired' rearranges IN PLACE into PLIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic machine such as a washer or toaster is a household device.

clue.text: Turns without the right and makes a beastly attack

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for turns goes round the letter

parts.note: in a game, your go is your turn, so turns are GOES
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone takes turns without going right and then lunges like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here means 'outside': GOES is wrapped round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A bull or boar pierces its victim with horns or tusks, which is what goring means.

clue.text: About a hundred and fifty intend to get back

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning, as in business letters
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to aim is to intend

explanation.surface: Somebody plans to recover roughly a hundred and fifty items.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something that was yours, such as luggage or land, is to take it back.

clue.text: The way to dress for discotheque lighting

parts.note: ST, street, is a way or road
a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: Advice on how to dress for a night at the disco.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs use a rapidly flashing lamp that freezes dancers' movements in bursts of light.

clue.text: Draw a circle around "Teetotal", plainly amused

indicators.note: around tells us the word for draw is placed about the abbreviation for teetotal

parts.note: a game ending level is a draw or tie
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: An instruction to ring the word 'Teetotal', with someone obviously giggling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; the quotation marks round 'Teetotal' make it look like a word to circle on a page, but it is just the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Giggling nervously or quietly is a visible sign that someone finds something funny.

clue.text: He has now changed — with some hesitation

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters of the little word are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A man has altered his position, though not without a moment's doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' signals the anagram; 'He has' reads as the start of a sentence, but together the two words define a possessor.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who possesses something, the one it belongs to, is its proprietor.

clue.text: One by one, the team appears

definitions.meaning: the figure one set beside another figure one makes the number written 11
a football or cricket side has this many players

explanation.walkthrough: 'One by one' sounds like 'singly', but it means two figure 1s side by side; 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side fields this number of players, so the word names the team itself.

clue.text: Lays into stylish parties

parts.note: in means fashionable or stylish
sets are groups or parties of people

explanation.surface: Someone launches an attack on fashionable social circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lays into' reads as 'attacks', but it means places one thing within another.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a smaller piece, such as a picture in a page, inside something is to set it in.

clue.text: A spill, to come to the point

definitions.meaning: a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper for lighting a fire or candle
to narrow gradually towards one end

explanation.walkthrough: 'come to the point' sounds like 'stop waffling', but means narrowing to a tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin wick used for lighting is a spill, and to narrow towards a tip is to come to a point.

clue.text: The woman is opposed to standing

parts.note: con, as in pros and cons, means against
a stance is a way of standing, or a position taken

explanation.surface: A woman who is against standing up.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue just wants a woman's name, and this one is a female given name.

clue.text: Bring back control —- the country's behind it

indicators.note: behind it means the second word follows the first in the answer

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
a state is a country; the 's is short for 'is'

explanation.surface: A call to restore authority, with the whole nation backing the move.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone or something to a former post or position is to return them to it.

clue.text: A hideout for potential high-fliers

parts.note: not a refuge for ambitious young executives but the nest where baby eagles are raised

explanation.walkthrough: 'High-fliers' suggests rising stars; the potential fliers are unfledged eaglets in their lofty nest.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest, high on a crag, is where chicks that will one day soar are raised.

clue.text: Establish a business after study

indicators.note: after places the word for a business after the word for study

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: Advice to set up a company once you've finished your studies.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify or settle something as true is to establish it.

clue.text: So-so tense

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense for continuous past action, as in 'I was walking'

explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like 'nervous', but it is the grammar term.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawed is only middling, and grammar names a past tense for unfinished action the same way.

clue.text: Turn a number back

parts.note: a spin is a turn
L is fifty in Roman numerals, a number

explanation.surface: An instruction to rotate a figure the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the instruction but is the definition, used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything relating to the backbone, as in a backbone injury, is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Assign property

definitions.meaning: to credit or ascribe something to a cause or person
a quality or characteristic of something

explanation.definitionFit: To credit something to a source is to ascribe it, and a characteristic quality is a property.

clue.text: A supporter is needed here and there perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the words before it are a possible arrangement of other letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is wanted to back things up in various places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges AND THERE; 'is needed here' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or devotee of a cause or person backs it, so is a supporter.

clue.text: The fellow going about very quietly is hot stuff!

indicators.note: going about means the word for fellow surrounds the musical mark

parts.note: a peer is a fellow or equal
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: A quiet man sneaking about is said to be rather a hot property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' signals the container; 'hot stuff' sounds like a compliment for an attractive person, but describes the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: This spice is fiery on the tongue, so literally hot stuff.

clue.text: Drill in the end made by farm machinery

indicators.note: in tells us the drill abbreviation sits inside the word for end

parts.note: the rear is the back end
PE, physical education, is drill or exercise

explanation.surface: Someone describes a tool's tip made by agricultural equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container and 'made by' is a link; 'Drill' suggests a boring tool next to the farm equipment, but is the school-exercise sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A harvesting machine that cuts crops is a piece of agricultural equipment.

clue.text: Saw the digs as arranged

indicators.note: as arranged tells us the letters before it are set out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone viewed the lodgings exactly as booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as arranged' rearranges THE DIGS ('digs' is British slang for lodgings).
explanation.definitionFit: To have caught sight of something is to have seen it.

clue.text: Few cut a trainee

parts.note: to sever is to cut
L, for learner, is a trainee, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: Only a few trimmed a novice's work.
explanation.definitionFit: A small number more than two is a handful, the same idea as a few.

clue.text: Given a gratuity which must be listed

definitions.meaning: handed a small extra payment for service
leaned over to one side, as a ship lists

explanation.walkthrough: 'listed' looks like 'recorded on a list', but it is the nautical sense of leaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiter handed extra money has been rewarded, and a leaning ship has tilted over.

clue.text: Not all but certain currencies suffer

indicators.note: not all but means only part of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Some currencies, but not all, endure losses.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring a cost or penalty on yourself, such as a loss, is to suffer it.

clue.text: Fowl is well covered

definitions.meaning: a castrated cockerel fattened for the table
read as two words, with a hat placed on top

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as CAP ON for the whimsical second sense: wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fattened castrated cock is a table bird, and with a cap on one is wearing a hat.

clue.text: Divers eat unrestrainedly, so puff

indicators.note: unrestrainedly suggests the letters before it run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Divers stuffing themselves without restraint, and so breathing hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puff' looks like panting, but it means to promote with praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To puff a product is to praise it extravagantly, which is to promote it publicly.

clue.text: Regret shown about church decoration

indicators.note: shown about means the word for regret is placed round the church abbreviation

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry about how a church has been decorated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown about' signals the container; 'church decoration' reads as one phrase, but the church is only part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered frill of fabric used to trim clothes is an ornamental trimming.

clue.text: The public are well aware that he manipulates the figures

definitions.text: The public are well aware that he manipulates the figures

parts.words: The public are well aware that he manipulates the figures
parts.note: not a statistician cooking the books but a showman whose audience openly watches him work little figures on strings

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests financial fiddling; the figures are dolls, and the audience knows full well who works them.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who works marionettes or glove dolls in front of an audience moves the figures by hand.

clue.text: Agent for the accountant to deal with

parts.note: CA, chartered accountant, is an accountant
to use something is to deal with or handle it

explanation.surface: Someone acts on behalf of the accountant in handling business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent' looks like a representative, but means something that brings about an effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever produces an effect is its agent, the thing that makes it happen.

clue.text: Get on in time and make a presentation

indicators.note: in means the little word is placed inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told to arrive punctually to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container and 'Get' is a link; 'presentation' suggests a talk, but means handing over a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To give money or goods to a cause is to present them as a gift.

clue.text: Fly from ordeal with utmost speed

parts.note: to fly is to flee or run away
a test is a trial or ordeal

explanation.surface: Someone escapes a gruelling trial as fast as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of fleet, meaning swift, describes the one moving most quickly.
